question: Should OpenClaw intentionally fail closed for byte-size CLI and config values above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` instead of preserving the previous rounded behavior?
rationale: Root policy treats stricter config validation as upgrade-sensitive, and this PR changes unsafe existing values from accepted or silently rounded to rejected even though the code fix is otherwise narrow.

options.title: Accept fail-closed guard
options.body: Treat unsafe byte-size values as invalid because JavaScript cannot represent them exactly, and merge after normal maintainer review.

options.title: Require upgrade proof
options.body: Ask for explicit fresh-install and existing-config proof that validation errors are clear before merging the stricter behavior.

options.title: Request compatibility path
options.body: Preserve old rounding behavior or add a migration path, at the cost of keeping precision-corrupted byte counts accepted longer.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed guard
recommendation.body: Treat unsafe byte-size values as invalid because JavaScript cannot represent them exactly, and merge after normal maintainer review.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame and the recent merged PR history make this the clearest owner for the touched parser/config files.
